name: Dull Dark Purple
lede: Dull Dark Purple is a muted, reddish purple first plated by Robert Ridgway in 1912, and nearly identical to the crowd-named Dirty Purple a century on.

sections.title: A 1912 plate, echoed by a 2010 survey
sections.body:
Ridgway's *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* of 1912 plates this swatch at plate XXVI, hue 67 prime, on an aged, scanned original that is itself approximate [1]. The name pairs *dull dark* with [[purple]] [1]. At hex #7B4A6C it measures lightness 38 and chroma 28 in LCH, and the nearest ISCC-NBS block reads as a moderate reddish purple, 7.2 units off [1].

Its closest named neighbors are [[dull-dark-purple|Dirty Purple]] and [[dusky-plum|Dusky Plum]], each 2.6 units away and almost the same color; [[dull-dark-purple|Dirty Purple]] comes from the unrelated 2010 xkcd survey, nearly a century after this plate, yet lands almost on top of it [2]. [[raisin-purple|Raisin Purple]] sits 3.1 units off, also almost the same [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This match appears in 0.02% of the 23,781 paintings in our archive (5 paintings, as photographed); the within-painting lens narrows that to 3 [3]. In our archive it is rarer than 79% of the named colors [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a shadow, in 33% of its 3 appearances by lightness rank within the painting [3]. The earliest match dates to 1600, 312 years before the name's 1912 record, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin and a look-alike hue in an aged photograph is not proof of a pigment or dye [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so the match is a screen comparison, not a pigment identification [3].
